name: GT3582 Street Billet Turbocharger
description: GT35/GT3582 frame turbocharger with a billet compressor wheel and cast turbine wheel, T3 4-bolt exhaust flange. This is a larger-frame unit built for higher airflow rather than fast spool.
recommendation: Best suited to 3.0L–5.0L V6/V8 engines targeting roughly 500–650 HP at 12–18 psi. The compressor housing is larger than what a small 4-cylinder can spool quickly — on a small engine this turbo will feel laggy. On a V6/V8 with enough exhaust volume to spin it, it delivers strong mid-range and top-end power for street/strip builds.
math_note: Sizing logic: larger compressor + turbine wheels flow more air but need more exhaust volume to spin up. Bigger displacement (more exhaust gas per revolution) spools a large frame like this faster than a small engine can.

name: GT3076 / GT3037 T3 V-Band Turbocharger
description: GT3037/GT3076 dual-designation turbo (compressor housing labeled GT3037, turbine GT3076) with a V-band turbine outlet, .82 A/R compressor and .60 A/R turbine.
recommendation: A good match for 2.0L–3.5L four- or six-cylinder engines targeting 350–500 whp. The .60 A/R turbine spools noticeably quicker than a larger-frame unit, making it a common choice for inline-4 and small V6 street/track builds that still want strong top-end.
math_note: Sizing logic: a .60 A/R turbine trades some ultimate top-end flow for quicker spool — the right trade-off for smaller-displacement engines that don't produce huge exhaust volume at low RPM.

name: S300SX3 / S366 Twin Scroll Turbocharger
description: S300SX3 / S366 twin-scroll turbocharger, .91 A/R T4 turbine housing. Manufacturer-listed range is broad (320–800 HP) because output depends heavily on A/R, boost level, and supporting mods.
recommendation: Best for larger 4-cylinder (2.0L+), V6, or V8 engines with a twin-scroll (divided) exhaust manifold, targeting high boost (20+ psi) race or drag applications. This is a large-frame turbo — on a small engine with a stock single-scroll manifold it won't see the spool benefit it's designed for, and will lag badly.
math_note: Sizing logic: twin-scroll design only pays off with a matching divided-manifold setup; without one, you lose the scavenging benefit that makes this turbo spool reasonably despite its size.

name: GT3076 / GT3037 Performance Turbocharger
description: GT3037/GT3076 frame turbo with a T3 4-bolt turbine flange (vs. V-band on the GEN2 version), .82 A/R compressor and .60 A/R turbine.
recommendation: Suited to 2.0L–3.5L turbo builds targeting a higher ceiling (up to ~600 HP) than the V-band version, while keeping reasonable spool. Good fit for aggressive standalone-tuned inline-4 or small V6 builds. Not recommended for larger V8 applications — the compressor will run out of efficient flow range before making use of a big engine's airflow needs.
math_note: Sizing logic: same frame as the GEN2 above, so the spool/displacement relationship is the same — this is a flange-style choice (T3 4-bolt vs V-band), not a different power class.

name: TO4E T3/T4 Stage III Turbocharger
description: T04E frame turbo on a T3/T4 hybrid flange, .57 A/R, oil-cooled only (no water cooling). Manufacturer-listed for 1.5L–2.5L engines, up to roughly 400 HP.
recommendation: Best fit for 1.5L–2.5L four-cylinder daily-driven or mild street builds at low-to-moderate boost (8–12 psi). Small compressor and tight .57 A/R mean quick spool on a small engine, but it will choke and become a restriction on anything V6 or larger.
math_note: Sizing logic: a .57 A/R is a small housing — great for quick spool on low-displacement engines, but it physically can't flow the air a bigger engine needs at higher RPM.

name: Universal Front Mount Intercooler Kit
description: Universal front-mount intercooler, 27" x 7" x 2.5" core, with a 2.5" aluminum piping kit included.
recommendation: A compact core sized for daily-driven or moderate street builds up to roughly 450–500 HP. Good fit for most 4-cylinder and smaller V6 turbo setups running moderate boost, where engine bay space is limited.
math_note: Sizing logic: core volume (L × W × thickness) roughly tracks heat-dissipation capacity — this core is on the smaller end, appropriate for lower sustained heat loads rather than repeated high-boost pulls.

name: Universal Performance Intercooler Kit
description: Universal front-mount intercooler, 31" x 13" x 3" core with 3" inlet/outlet, includes a 2.5" aluminum piping kit.
recommendation: A large core built for high-HP builds up to roughly 700–800 HP, or for engines seeing repeated high-boost pulls (drag or road course use) where sustained heat soak matters. Reasonable fit for larger displacement or heavily boosted 4-cylinder, V6, or V8 builds pairing with a bigger turbo like the S366 or GT3582 above.
math_note: Sizing logic: roughly 2.5x the core volume of the smaller intercooler above, meaning meaningfully more surface area to shed heat — matched to a bigger turbo pushing more mass airflow.

name: Universal T3/T4 TO4E Complete Turbocharger Kit
description: Complete T3/T4 T04E turbo kit for 1.5L–3.0L engines — includes the T04E turbocharger plus supporting hardware as a bundle.
recommendation: Best for first-time turbo builds on 1.5L–3.0L four-cylinder engines wanting an all-in-one starting point. Same T04E sizing logic as the standalone unit above — quick spool on smaller engines, not a fit for V6/V8 applications.
math_note: Sizing logic: identical frame/flow characteristics to the standalone T04E .57 A/R above — the kit just bundles the supporting parts.

name: 5-Piece T3 TO4E 420HP Turbo Upgrade Kit
description: 5-piece T3 T04E 420HP turbo upgrade kit for 3.0L–5.0L engines — bundles the turbo with oil feed/return lines and intercooler piping.
specs: Kit includes: Turbo, oil feed/return lines, intercooler piping
recommendation: Suited to 3.0L–5.0L six- or eight-cylinder engines targeting a moderate, reliable power bump (up to ~420 HP) rather than a maximum-effort build. The included plumbing makes this a reasonable one-box option for a first turbo install on a larger engine.
math_note: Sizing logic: same T04E frame as the smaller kit above, but the 420 HP ceiling reflects it being matched here to larger-displacement engines that can support that output at moderate boost.

name: FLF AN Female to AN Male with 1/8" NPT Port Adapter - 06 AN
description: Finish Line Factory's AN Female to AN Male with 1/8" NPT Port Adapter is perfect for situations where you need to quickly add a port for a sensor or tap into a line for a liquid or air feed. These CNC machined from high-quality 6061 aluminum and designed for high performance applications.
recommendation: Precision CNC machined high-performance component engineered by Finish Line Factory. Ideal for custom fuel, oil, coolant, or air plumbing.
math_note: Standard high-flow AN / NPT thread specifications for reliable sealing and minimum fluid restriction.
